conventions.convention: Scalars form a field k; tensor products are algebraic over k, every tensor expression is a finite sum, and reassociation uses the canonical associators and unit maps.
Bialgebras have unital associative multiplication and counital coassociative comultiplication; both Δ and ε are unital algebra homomorphisms. Tensor-product multiplication is componentwise.
Convolution is f*g = m_A(f⊗g)Δ_C, with unit u_A ε_C; it is distinct from ordinary composition.
An antipode is a linear two-sided convolution inverse of the identity. Compositional bijectivity is not part of the definition.
The full function-algebra construction k^G uses finite G. The group-algebra construction permits arbitrary G. The polynomial construction works in every characteristic.
Commutativity and cocommutativity are separate sufficient hypotheses for S² = id.
Permutation products apply the rightmost permutation first; for a=(12), b=(23), ab=(123) and ba=(132).

load_bearing.statement: A Hopf algebra over k is a bialgebra H with a k-linear map S satisfying S*id_H = uε = id_H*S. This definition imposes no compositional bijectivity condition on S.
For a Hopf algebra H over a field, the antipode S is unique, S(1)=1, ε∘S=ε, S(ab)=S(b)S(a), and Δ(S(h))=(S⊗S)τΔ(h). These follow from the convolution-inverse definition.

For a k-coalgebra C and a unital associative k-algebra A, convolution f*g=m_A(f⊗g)Δ_C is a well-defined associative multiplication on Hom_k(C,A), with two-sided unit u_A ε_C, without finite-dimensionality assumptions.

A bialgebra combines a unital associative k-algebra and a counital coassociative k-coalgebra, requiring Δ and ε to be unital algebra homomorphisms. A bialgebra map preserves multiplication, unit, comultiplication, and counit.
For k-coalgebras C,D, the coproduct Δ(c⊗d)=Σ(c₁⊗d₁)⊗(c₂⊗d₂) and counit ε(c⊗d)=ε_C(c)ε_D(d) define a coalgebra on C⊗D, without finite-dimensionality assumptions.

Over any field k, kG is Hopf for any group G with Δ(g)=g⊗g, ε(g)=1, S(g)=g⁻¹; k^G is Hopf for finite G with Δ(f)(x,y)=f(xy), ε(f)=f(e), S(f)(x)=f(x⁻¹); k[x] is Hopf with x primitive and S(x)=-x. In characteristic p>0, x^p is also primitive.

Unital associative algebra structures, central scalar maps, bilinear multiplication, and unital algebra homomorphisms.
Existence and composition laws for tensor products of linear maps.
Tensor-unit contractions and the multiplication identification k⊗k → k.
Componentwise multiplication and unit on tensor-product algebras.
Construction of kG with basis G and unique finite coefficient expressions.
Unique linear extension of structure maps prescribed on group or monomial bases.
Descent of bilinear multiplication pairings to linear maps on tensor products.
Finite function-space tensor identification and nonvanishing of the polynomial basis tensor x⊗x.
Free associative algebra and quotient presentation of the group algebra.
Monomial basis and generator universal property of k[x]. The Laurent and fraction-field conclusions are not needed by this batch.

seams_checked.note: The coalgebra and coalgebra-map equations match the opened supplier Definition, including both counit equations and canonical associators. The primitive-element use specifies the group-like unit. These uses do not invoke the supplier page's AC-dependent coalgebra theorems.

This is a page-level prerequisite without an assigned-item logical dependency on that page. Its opened right-comodule and dual-convolution definitions use compatible tensor and convolution orders; no finite-dimensional duality or rationality conclusion is imported into the batch's arbitrary-dimensional convolution proof.

Dual, quotient, kernel, tensor-product, finite-dual, and Taft consumers preserve the bialgebra and two-sided antipode interfaces. Map–antipode commutation uses uniqueness in Hom(H,K) convolution. Full duality is restricted to finite dimension, and finite-dual closure uses anti-multiplicativity without assuming S bijective.

The diagonal action uses the stated bialgebra equations. Left duals use S and the two antipode contractions without bijectivity. Right duals explicitly assume bijective S before using S⁻¹; the bidual formula retains the S² twist.

The coinvariant projection uses precisely ΔS=(S⊗S)τΔ, S(1)=1, and the two antipode contractions. The decomposition proof uses anti-multiplicativity and does not introduce S⁻¹ or a dimension restriction.

The regular-dual Hopf-module calculation and averaging argument use the supplied anti-map and contraction identities with their stated orders. Finite-dimensional antipode bijectivity is proved downstream rather than attributed to the general antipode theorem; Maschke does not infer general involutivity.

The opened quasitriangular definition and counit/Yang–Baxter lemma use the Hopf algebra's unital bialgebra and counit equations faithfully. The R tensor is explicitly algebraic and finite; its invertibility is a separate quasitriangular hypothesis.

The consumers preserve convolution order, anti-multiplication, anti-comultiplication, and εS=ε. They distinguish H*op from a reversed coproduct. Uses of S⁻¹ have explicit bijectivity hypotheses and a separate finite-dimensional bijectivity supplier.

The quantum-antipode descent lemma states the same two-sided antipode interface explicitly, without asserting bijectivity. It checks relation descent and both contractions on generators, then extends them to words by anti-multiplicativity and bialgebra compatibility; it does not infer an antipode from the bialgebra structure alone.
